1. My daughter, a line to ask you to buy everything on this little list.2 If you can, send it all at once.

2. I am on my feet as God wills. Pray and have others pray, for charity's sake, for this is a time of adversity. As soon as I have a moment I will write to you at length.

Greet everyone for me; God bless you; I am

your poor MOTHER

1 The date is derived from two facts: the Mother's departure

for Nizza on 2.11, and Sr. A. Francesca's reply to this letter on 4.11.72.

2 She asked for paper and books (needed for the school) and linen. Cf. L Ra-

pallino to Camisa, 6.11.72.

In reply to his request, she sets out the indispensable conditions she lays down for accepting the nursing of her Religious in hospitals. She is willing to discuss it in person while she is in Nizza.

Reverend Sir,

1. I reply to your esteemed letter, giving you all the explanations Your Reverence asks of me regarding the functions of our Institute and what is required for nursing in hospitals.1

2. If the Hospital calls the Sisters to nurse, the least that can be done for them would be 400 F. each and firewood.2

3. Then, since we have the obligation of home nursing, the Sisters who are to carry out this office remain at the charge of our Institute.

4. If, on the other hand, it is to be arranged differently,3 by entrusting us with a sum for the maintenance of the sick, then it would have been better to discuss this in person, and it would give me great pleasure to have the good fortune of seeing you while I am in Nizza, so as to settle everything face to face.

5. I shall stay here until next Saturday, the 9th of this month, after which I shall go to Piacenza.

6. I take this opportunity to offer you my most respectful greetings and ask your blessing, while I sign myself Your Reverence's

Most humble Sr. ANNA MARIA ROSA GATTORNO

1 Don Tito Borgatta had written to her on 29 October. AFSA G 9, 5.

2 An annual stipend of 400 francs, and firewood for heating and cooking.

3 Arranged differently, that is, the administration and responsibility for the services.

She has been in Piacenza a few hours. Sorry not to have found him to talk in person, she writes. She has sorrows and tribulations in plenty, but she is content on the cross. The day will come when they end, and for her too — she will not doubt it — there will be beatitude in Paradise.

A.M.F.

My Father Agostino,

1. I arrived in Piacenza only a few hours ago, and since I did not have the good fortune of finding you and talking with you in person, I do so in writing.1

2. So many sorrows! so many tribulations! they are drowning me; and why all this? alas, I know the cause: this infamous woman deserves it all.2 So often in my grief I say to myself: "O prisons, why do you delay to bind me in your fetters? at least I would have peace and could be with the only One I know for myself and find all my consolation in Him".3

3. Alas! I am all too well on the cross, but these bones are wasting away day by day, and my skeleton is beginning to frighten me.4

4. Good Father Agostino, forgive me if I cause you melancholy with these sad thoughts; the blessed day when we shall go to our Homeland in Paradise; but as for the thought that a day must come when my tribulations will end, I don't know, I would almost say [I have] a doubt that for me it will not come; and this because the gate of hell will open for me.5

5. But no, no! I will not go on.6 I will stop my pen and bring it to its proper end. Meanwhile pray, as

this poor creature prays every day for her Father Agostino.

Bless me and believe me ever your unworthy

Sr. ANNA MARIA ROSA GATTORNO

1 Only a few hours ago... On arrival she had learned that Fr Agostino had left on the

morning of that same day. Cf. L Francesca Camisa to M. Rosa 8.11.72.

2 ...sorrows, tribulations are drowning me: they take my breath away. A vivid image

that conveys the kind and amount of sorrow well. One had wounded her particu-

larly: the loss of Sr. A. Serafina Lorenzi on 30 October 1872. Cf. L 319, 1.

3 She calls on the "fetters", the chains of imprisonment which, by physically confining her,

would cut her off from the outside world and make easier the encounter with the One she knows

and in whom she finds all consolation.

4 ...to frighten me: to disturb me by its extreme frailty.

5 She fears that because of her unworthiness eternal suffering

awaits her.

6 It is a temptation and a cause of suffering, so she stops writing and ends

trusting in his prayer.

She should ask Don Accinelli how to handle the benefactors' gifts. The sick are God's blessing. She should go forward with courage.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

My daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

1. Listen, before I forget: give the list of subscribers to Sr. A. Eletta, because those of Sestri are on it and they go to them; show it to Don Accinelli and tell him how the people who give to you can be divided from those of S. P. d'Arena.1

2. I have just received yours and am very glad of all you write; the Lord bless you.2 Your sister is much better; Sr. A. Crocifissa so-so; so far nothing can be said.3 I will send you the nurses on Wednesday.4 I would like to know whether you have yet collected enough for flour, because I always worry about this.5 Try to give as much as you can to Don Accinelli; it will go for flour.

3. Listen, the old watch that belonged to the Superior: did you perhaps exchange that too? If not, keep it and exchange it as soon as you can, for I need one, since you have taken them all from me; don't worry about it.

4. How glad I am to hear that you have patients. What a blessing, my dear daughter! Courage; don't forget to go to Angelo Burgo about the Chapel.6 The rest I have writ-

ten to Don Accinelli. Goodbye; greet everyone for me, and you, my dear daughter, receive in the Heart of Jesus a thousand blessings that I implore for you from this Most Sacred Heart; I am

your affectionate MOTHER ROSA

1 ...the list of subscribers. A number of well-to-do gentlemen had

joined a subscription promoted by M. Rosa for the benefit of her Sisters' works,

each undertaking to pay annually the sum he had freely

pledged (Cf. L 90, 4 and L Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti to M. Rosa, 6 August 1871).

Sr. A. Eletta Bruschi, Superior of the House at Sampierdarena.

2 ...I have just received. In her letter of 12.11 Sr. A. Santina reported

on the house and the nursing of the sick, writing among other things: (the patients) "They are so

pleased... they praise the nurses so much".

3 Her blood sister: Sr. A. Ermelinda Solenghi had been in Piacenza for some

time for her health; Sr. A. Crocifissa Fiocchi, who had gone there a few days earlier on

Don Accinelli's advice, because she too was unwell, was in a sta-

tionary condition. (Cf. L Sr. A. Santina Solenghi to M. Rosa of 11.11.1872).

4 More nurses were needed for the growing number of patients to be

cared for. On Don Accinelli's advice she had had to ask for four Sisters from the

Sampierdarena community to meet the families' requests. (Cf.

L Sr. A. Santina to M. Rosa 11.11.1872).

5 "...whether you have collected. The Sisters lived by begging.

6 Angelo Burgo, a benefactor. Cf. L 24.

She is unable to meet the expenses of maintaining the 50 girls orphaned by cholera. She requests a subsidy.

Most Illustrious Prefect,

1. The undersigned is compelled to make known to Your Illustrious Lordship the wretched position of this poor house1 regarding the fifty little girls orphaned by cholera placed here by the Honourable Municipality, all of them poor.

2. Since provisions have been so dear in these years and we have no subsidies, I must give notice that unless Your Illustrious Lordships come to our aid with at least the sum of 1000 F., I am forced, to my regret, to tell you that I must send them back to the Municipality.2 I can keep them no longer.

I beg Your Illustrious Lordships,3 in the name of these poor children, to help them soon.

I have the honour to sign myself Your Illustrious Lordships'

Most humble Sr. A. M. ROSA GATTORNO

1 ...wretched position: they lived very poorly and could never

free themselves of the debts owed to the suppliers of basic necessities.

2 Firm and resolute, she knows how to defend the rights of the poor and to remind those whose

duty it is to carry out the tasks that fall to them.

3 She also addresses the provincial administration.

She cannot bear the expense of the more than fifty girls housed in the Institute. She requests a subsidy.

Most Illustrious Mayor,

1. The undersigned is compelled to make known to Your Illustrious Lordships1 the wretched position of this poor house2 regarding the fifty little girls orphaned by cholera whom Your Illustrious Lordships placed here, to whom for six years now I have provided board and education; moreover, to the number of girls mentioned are added other little ones, who are a very heavy burden, and since provisions are so dear it is impossible for me to keep them any longer. Unless Your Illustrious Lordships help me by giving me the sum of 1000 F. as soon as possible, I am forced, against my will, to send them all back to the Municipality.3

In the name, then, of these poor children, I beg Your Illustrious Lordships to help them soon, while I have the honour to sign myself

Your Illustrious Lordships' most humble Sr. ANNA M. R. G.

1 She also addresses the members of the Municipal Council.

2 Cf. L 324, n. 1.

3 ...I am forced. The strong, brisk manner expresses the strong moral fibre of

M. Rosa, who knows how to threaten in defence of the rights of the poor, but also how

to plead and ask for prompt help.

She is pleased with her work and encourages her to labour for the Lord.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

My daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

1. A line, dear daughter, to tell you I am pleased with your work. Forward, courage; attend to observance and to the report.1

2. My dear, I am delighted to hear that providence is coming; what a blessing! Take heart and work for the Lord. God will repay you. I'll be with you soon. Goodbye; everything in person.

I am your affectionate M. ROSA

1 The "dear daughter" wrote to her almost every day to keep her informed about the running of the house, the service to the sick and anything else that might please the Mother. The other Superiors likewise gave her the "report" she wanted.

She suggests rules of personal conduct in her task as Superior and instructs her on how to treat the Sisters and run the Community.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

My daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

1. I have received your letter; now pay attention: First: I want you to go straight to bed in the evening after the rosary, and the sisters must be quite convinced that you do. Second: be first at meditation. Third: at all exercises of piety; take great care not to show favouritism,1 not to tell the sisters you know their faults because you read them in their hearts;2 not to make them deny their own will too much, lest they lose their vocation. In these matters one must leave it to the Superiors.3

2. You must not call the sisters or require them to come every day to see whether they may receive Communion the next day; once only, on Sunday, they are to ask you. And you will tell them yes or no, as you think fit.4

3. For charity's sake, I urge you not to run into debt, for, as you saw, the one before you did not;5 so I want it to be the same with you.

4. I commend to you the schools and the care of the boarders; the observance of the Holy Rules. We must [try] to give no occasion for any singularity, spiritual or temporal,

so that the sisters may imitate us not in the extraordinary but in the exact observance of the Holy Rules.

The Lord guide you and comfort you in all things. I am your

Affectionate M. ROSA

1 ...not to show favouritism: treat the Sisters even-handedly, without

favourites.

2 ...read in their hearts: that would be presumption and undue arbitrariness.

3 ...not to make them deny: she should act with the utmost respect and discretion, leaving

to the Mother responsibility for decisions in important cases.

4 Asking the Superior's permission to receive Communion was one of the Church

regulations of the time. In the Family it was the practice to ask for it week-

ly: "...on Sunday each Sister will come to ask you (the Superior) per-

mission to receive Communion during the week". Appl. Reg. Del., n. 28.

5 The previous Superior: Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni.

She is glad of the news of the good journey. She comforts her, urging her to remain always in the presence of God the Father and remember her instructions. She is close to her.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

My good and beloved daughter,

1. A few hours ago I received your letter; I am glad to hear of your good journey; it could not have been otherwise. I am glad you were able to arrive before the Countess.1

2. By now you will already have done battle.2 Don't forget to remain always in the presence of God the Father; remember the instructions this wretch gave you. I am with you and mean never to abandon you.

3. This morning many prayers were said for the Countess, that God may enlighten her and make her know the truth. Provided it pleases this good Father.

4. My beloved daughter, listen, I write no more for now, but when I receive your next letter I will answer again.

Goodbye; may the Lord pour out on you his choicest blessings. I am for ever your

Affectionate MOTHER ROSA

1 ...that you made. Sr. A. Vincenza was accompanying Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti,

the Community's new Superior, replacing Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni.

Countess Maria Anna Trotti was also to go there. Cf. L 318, n. 1.

2 ...done battle. She was to speak plainly to the Countess, defending

the Sisters, whom the steward accused of having damaged the furnishings of the

house.

The Sacred Congregation has not accepted the second Rules. She would like Fr Fava to come to the Mother House before drawing up others.

1. Last night I received the letter from Mgr Mariano informing me that the Sacred Congregation has sent back the second Rules3 and that Your Eminence is of the opinion that others should be drawn up and composed by [Father] Fava.4

2. Your Eminence, if you will permit, I will set out my poor, humble view, which is that Father Fava should come here to the Mother House to observe how everything is run and on that basis draw up the Constitutions.5

3. I would come to Rome at once, but my poor health does not allow it at present; Your Eminence, I cannot but express to you the sorrow I felt [...].

1 Autograph draft lacking addressee, date and conclusion. It is a docu-

ment of considerable historical importance for the history of the

Rules. The addressee is inferred from the context.

2 The date is fixed by Mgr Mariano Wan-

stienkist's (Secretary to Cardinal Vannicelli) reply to it of 6 December 1872: "...on re-

ceiving your most esteemed and welcome letter of the 4th inst....". AFSA,

VW, 1872.

3 On 1 December '72 Mgr Mariano had informed her that he had looked into,

on Cardinal Vannicelli's behalf, the well-known matter of the Rules and had learned from

the Consultor Fr Bianchi, to whom the Rule had been entrusted for examination, that

he had returned it to the S. Congregation "with all the adverse

observations...".

4 The same Monsignor also conveyed to her the view of Mgr Vitelle-

schi and other dignitaries of the S. Congregation, summing it up thus:

"Since everything has to be changed, and to reach a conclusion, the Rules of the Dorotheans could be taken as a model for the education of Girls... and for the nursing of the Sick... the Rules of the Franciscans called Stigmatines... and the holy and learned Jesuit religious Fr Leonardo Fava would be most suitable for drawing up these Rules" (ibid.).

5 M. Rosa's view springs from a deep need for fidelity to the charism: the Rules had to express the life of the Family of Saint Anne, shaped by its own genuine spirit and not derived from outside bodies and systems.

She has done everything well. She is to present the new Superior, Sr. A. Paola, to the Community and leave her free to act, correcting her if necessary. The Mother would gladly go to greet the Countess but is prevented; she is determined to go and see her for a day.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

My dear daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

1. Last night I received yours; I did not answer at once because I had to reply to Mgr Mariano. My dear, I can tell you nothing except: wounds on every side.1

2. My Vincenza, come soon. Everything in person. I hear what you did; all is well.2 God bless you for ever; rest assured that every step will be repaid.

3. Now read two lines to the Religious and install Sr. A. Paola as Superior.3 Before you leave, it is good for you to see how she acts and let her get on with it, only correcting her where you see she falls short.

4. Listen, urge her not to form alliances with priests; in short, without my going on about it, you know everything.

5. So tell the Countess that for the moment I cannot leave this house; I am expecting someone who is coming to discuss the hospital and finish the arrangements, because Father Paolo would be too upset if he had to telegraph this Priest not to come;4 but sooner than the Countess5 I will come for a day and

then return, as I shall certainly do on Monday or Tuesday, for I absolutely want to see and embrace her.

6. I close because there are people here and I want you to receive this. You know, Vincenza, those two round ones,6 you understand me, the ones that are ours, like those in the guest quarters: I want them for the school, if you understand me.

Goodbye, dear daughter; I hold you to the Heart of Jesus. This morning's Communion was for you. For ever and eternally your

Most affectionate ROSA

1 Cf. L 329.

2 In her letter of 3 December she had told her in detail about her conversations

with Countess Maria Anna Trotti.

3 Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti. Cf. L 327.

4 This is Don Tito Borgatta, with whom she was to agree the terms of service

of the Sisters at the Ovada Hospital. Cf. L 317, 1; 321.

5 ...sooner: before the Countess is upset at not having had

her wish to see me granted, I will come...

6 ...so round: perhaps ornamental plates.

She urges her not to worry; she does not write only because she is very busy. News of the health of two sisters; she urges silence.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

My daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

1. Just a line to tell you that you must not worry when I don't write, because you have no reason to, since I wrote telling you to be of good heart; moreover Sr. A. Vincenza has been in Ferrara for several days. So you see this should be enough to show how busy I am.

2. I hear about the sick sister; let us hope she recovers.1 Here Sr. A. Crocifissa is very well and has been losing her nights for several days; Sr. Ermelinda is better, though she still suffers climbing the stairs, but she is putting on weight.2

3. Try to do well, and in particular I urge silence on you; and no shouting during recreation, lest people say you are bad nuns. For charity's sake, I urge strict and mitigated silence, and the report too; silence in the streets — for charity's sake let them not talk, but keep silence; remember that if your superiors are not there, your Jesus is, walking behind you and counting all your steps. Be very careful: God sees you everywhere; so courage, and try always to keep your eyes fixed on God, our all.3

I am your affectionate MOTHER

Greet all the Sisters for me. God bless you all, and you a [...]

1 ...the sick sister. Sr. A. Marcellina had been in bed for some time. Cf. Let-

ters of Sr. A. Santina Solenghi: 1, 5, 6 December 1872.

2 ...losing her nights: she nurses the sick in their homes at night. Cf. L 323, 2.

3 ...try always to keep, etc.: crowning the preceding advice is the

recommendation that is as it were the soul of the Daughters of Saint Anne's activity: the

contemplative gaze that draws from God the love of complacency by which He alone is

all.

4 ...the conclusion is missing.

Courage, and always forward! Sr. A. Vincenza is in Ferrara and perhaps the Mother will go too. She asks him to get her two pictures of the Sacred Heart of Jesus, one for Nizza and the other for Ferrara. When will he call her to work in Rome with her Daughters?

A.M.F.

My good Father Agostino,

1. The moment I have a free minute I use it to write to you. Well, are we in battle? Courage, good weapons and fire at the ready, forward!1

2. This morning I saw Countess Caracciolo, all kindness. What a dear creature! And Father Cirillo too.2

3. Sr. A. Vincenza is in Ferrara; she went to receive the Countess. Perhaps on Monday I shall go too, and then return here to Piacenza on Saturday, since the girls' retreat is on Sunday.3

4. Now, my good Father, I ask you a favour, or rather an alms: to get me two [pictures of the] Sacred Heart of Jesus like those you sent me;4 if you could see how well it looks on the high altar! It was put there and will never be removed; likewise at S. P. d'Arena. Of these two, one should be for Nizza and the other for Ferrara.

5. You know that good creature5 will do nothing for the Church and I have to see to everything myself; I have everything, but I lack the picture for the second altar, and I want it to be the Sacred Heart.

6. When will you call me to Rome? Try to arrange that we may soon come and work in that city too.

7. My health is very bad; it does not allow me to go

on writing. When Sr. A. Vincenza comes, if I go to Ferrara, I will have her write to you; certainly if I feel so ill I shall not go. A word for me to St Francis, and believe me for ever

Your humble obedient Sr. A. M. ROSA G.

1 She alludes to the Rules, which were not approved. Cf. L 329.

2 Countess Isabella Caracciolo, a friend of Fr Agostino. Father Cirillo: cf. L

180, n. 5.

3 Perhaps on Monday: cf. L 330, 5.

4 Cf. L 224, n. 1.

5 Countess Maria Anna Trotti.

In two days she will be in Ferrara; she should tell the Countess. She is always close to her. She should take care of herself.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

My beloved daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

1. Yesterday I received yours; I hear everything and am very glad that, as you tell me, things are going well. Listen, unless you hear otherwise, on Tuesday by the train at one-something I shall be in Ferrara; tell the Countess.1 I don't write at length because I want you to have these two lines of mine; know that I am always with you; take care of yourself and mind your cough.

I am in a hurry; yours eternally, MOTHER ROSA

1 ...Tuesday, 10 December. Cf. L 330, n. 5.

She begs that the copy of the unapproved Constitutions be handed to Father Leonardo Fava SJ.

Most Reverend Excellency,

1. Sr. Anna Maria Rosa Gattorno, Foundress of the Charitable Institute of the Daughters of Saint Anne, humbly begs Your Most Reverend Excellency to deign to permit the copy of the Constitutions submitted to the S. Congregation of Bishops and Regulars, which was not approved, to be examined by the Rev. Fr Fava of the Society of Jesus so that he may draw up another Rule, correcting the defects found in the first.2

In this hope [...]

1 Place and date are inferred, the first from the context, the second from the office

register, in which we read: "By higher order not only was the enclosed copy re-

turned, but a summary of the observations on the Con-

stitutions was also given".

2 Cf. L 329.

She offers Christmas and New Year greetings and asks a blessing, as in the past, for the House about to be opened.

Most Reverend Eminence,

1. Please accept just a line from one who humbly offers you, with all the outpouring of her soul, greetings for the Holy Feasts and good wishes for a new year full of grace and happiness; and I pray that God may leave the Church a Prince of such Holiness and zeal. Ah! if my prayers are heard, you will be among us a hundred years.

2. Never having been accustomed in the past to open Houses1 without first asking Your Most Reverend Eminence's pastoral blessing, this seventh would seem less worthy to me if I did not do so.2

3. Most Reverend Eminence, bless then this poor daughter of Saint Anne and the whole Community, as I kneel to kiss your hand, signing myself with the greatest veneration Your Most Reverend Eminence's

Most humble Sr. ANNA MARIA ROSA GATTORNO

1 Cf. L 4.

2 The seventh house, at Ovada, a hospital. The other six in chronological order of

foundation:

- Piacenza, Mother House (1866);

- Sampierdarena, Orphanage (1868);

- Piacenza, Boys' School (1870);

- Genoa, home nursing of the sick (1871);

- Ferrara, boarding house for girls and School (1871);

- Nizza, hospital and schools (1872).

Negotiations are complete for opening a new Community at the Ovada Hospital at the beginning of the new year. She asks a blessing on the new work.

Most Reverend Eminence,

1. The great care and charitable interest you have taken in our poor Institute have laid the strictest obligation on the poor Daughters of Saint Anne to number you among their distinguished Benefactors, so that special prayers rise to God every day for your welfare.

2. In these days we have reached agreement with the Ovada Hospital, and after New Year's Day we shall go and take possession.1

3. May Your Most Reverend Eminence deign to bless this new work, that it may be pleasing to God and profitable to our souls, and give this wretch strength to work according to God's will, while, kissing your Sacred Purple, she remains Your Most Reverend Eminence's

Most humble Sr. A. ROSA GATTORNO

1 Cf. L 317, 1; 321; 330, n. 4; 335, n. 2.

She offers Christmas greetings, thanks him for his interest in the Institute's Rules and says she is glad of the invitation to come to Rome in January about them. She asks a blessing on the seventh House about to be opened.

Most Reverend Excellency,

1. A most just duty obliges me to express the gratitude I feel towards Your Most Reverend Excellency, and I am greatly consoled to be able with this letter to offer you greetings for the Holy Feasts and wishes for a new year full of grace and fully satisfying Your Excellency's desires.

2. I will not dwell on our business of the Rules; I only thank you infinitely, reserving the better expression of my gratitude for when we meet,1 having heard from Monsignor Mariano that I am to come to Rome in January; if God gives me a little health I will fly there with all my heart.2

3. Meanwhile please bless me in the new undertaking of a foundation, the Seventh House, which will be in a few days.3 Bless also this poor daughter of Saint Anne and all the Communities, as I kneel to receive it, while I am honoured to sign myself Your Most Reverend Excellency's

Most humble Sr. ANNA MARIA ROSA GATTORNO

1 Cf. L 329, n. 4.

2 Mgr Mariano Wanstienkist, Secretary to Cardinal Vannicelli, had in

fact written to her on 18 December: "...I believe your coming to

Rome will be indispensable, but not before 10 January".

3 Cf. L 336, n. 1.

For his fatherly and attentive interest on behalf of the Institute he is numbered among its distinguished benefactors; so every day, and especially as Christmas approaches, prayers are said for him.

Most Reverend Excellency,

1. The great care and charitable interest you have taken in our poor Institute have laid the strictest obligation on the poor Daughters of Saint Anne to number you among their distinguished benefactors, so that special prayers rise to God every day for your welfare, and especially in these holy days, that the Child may fill you with graces. In these days we have reached agreement with the Ovada Hospital, and after New Year's Day we shall go and take possession.1

2. May Your Most Reverend Excellency deign to bless this new work, that it may be pleasing to God and profitable to our souls, and give this wretch strength to work according to God's will.

Most Reverend Excellency, deign also to bless the whole Institute, and in particular her who signs herself Your Most Reverend Excellency's

Most humble Sr. A. ROSA GATTORNO

1 This is the seventh House. Cf. L 335, n. 2.

She sends New Year greetings in her own name and the Community's.

Most Reverend Excellency,

1. A just duty moves me to send Your Most Reverend Excellency wishes for prosperity in the coming new year, together with this poor Community, born in Your Excellency's flock — the last and lowliest of all.

2. I trust that, as our Shepherd, you will not disdain to accept from your humble and poor daughter the prayers she raises to God every day, together with the whole Community, that you may live a long series of years among us.

Kneeling at your feet, awaiting Your Most Reverend Excellency's blessing, is

your most humble daughter and servant Sr. A. M. R. G.

She blesses her and the Community and urges her to go and pay her respects to the auxiliary Bishop. She has done everything well.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

My daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

1. A line in my own hand to wish you from heaven all the choicest blessings on you and your Community; and meanwhile I let you know that it is good for you to go to Mgr Giordani, the Bishop. Sr. A. Domenica knows where to go, in the curia; he acts for the Archbishop.1

2. And then let everyone try to write to the Father.2 For the rest, I have no remarks on anything you write. You did very well with Giovanna.3

3. Goodbye; don't think this note too short, but I have too many occupations; they steal all [my time].

Goodbye; I leave you in Jesus, calling myself your

Affectionate MOTHER ROSA

1 Mgr Luigi Giordani was coadjutor Bishop to Cardinal Luigi Vanni-

celli, Archbishop of Ferrara. Since she is new to the place, the Mother tells her to

go in person to pay her respects and offer Christmas greetings.

2 Father G. B. Tornatore.

3 The Superior had advised Sr. A. Giovanna Bixio how to deal

with her brother regarding the letter with the money order he sent her periodically. Cf. L

Bucciotti to M. Rosa, 23 December 1872 and L 158, n. 12.

She had a good journey; they should thank God; she thanks everyone for their prayers.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

PRESENTAZIONE

Buon interprete del Concilio Vaticano II e delle sue consegne riguardanti il rinnovamento della vita religiosa, il P. Elio Gambari ci ricorda nel suo Manuale della Vita Religiosa alla luce del Vaticano II che «la fedeltà ai Fondatori/alle Fondatrici è uno dei principi fondamentali del rinnovamento. Nel Fondatore/nella Fondatrice l'Istituto ritrova se stesso, la propria individualità o identità e il proprio dinamismo» (Cap. X, p. 77).

Orbene, una buona strada e forse la migliore tra le tante altre possibili per vivere in fedeltà ai Fondatori/alle Fondatrici consiste nel conoscere i loro scritti, le loro lettere dove questi trasmettono ai loro interlocutori qualcosa di se stessi, i loro ideali, le loro aspirazioni profonde, il loro pensiero, la loro brama di lavorare instancabilmente per la gloria di Dio, il servizio della Chiesa ed il bene dei fratelli.

Consapevoli di questa realtà le Figlie di S. Anna, per mantenersi sempre più fedeli alla loro Fondatrice, proseguono con encomiabile spirito di Famiglia la pubblicazione delle lettere di M. Gattorno. Nel mese di giugno ci offrivano in dono il 2" volume delle lettere scritte da M. Rosa dal 1871 al 1872; oggi ci fanno il dono di un altro volume, il 3° della serie, che abbraccia il biennio successivo.

Nelle lettere raccolte in questo 3" volume M. Gattorno continua a rivelarsi, come già veniva da me accennato nella presentazione del precedente, donna di «affascinante e travolgente personalità umana e mistica... sposa, mamma e fondatrice... ricca del senso delicatamente umano di una Santa Teresa d'Avila e allo stesso tempo della calorosa ispirazione mistica della grande riformatrice del Carmelo».

Le lettere di questo 3" volume hanno qualcosa di caratteristico che avvalora in modo particolare il loro interesse a la loro importanza. Furono scritte in uno dei momenti emergenti della vita e dell'opera della Fondatrice: il quadriennio (1871-1874) chiamato dalla compilatrice Sr. Anna Maria E. Convertini il periodo «dell'evoluzione iniziale della Famiglia nella concretizzazione strutturale delle comunità, dei servizi caritativi e della tensione spirituale di M. Rosa originata dall'ardente desiderio di vedere la Famiglia inserita nella 'vita della Chiesa' mediante l'approvazione delle regole».

In questo periodo della evoluzione e concretizzazione strutturale dell'Istituto M. Rosa ebbe a sopportare un vero martirio tante volte paragonabile alle sofferenze di Gesù dal Getsemani al Calvario. Difatti in parecchie lettere sembra sentire l'eco della tensione esistenziale in cui

visse. Un esempio lo abbiamo quando, scrivendo al Cardinal Vicario Costantino Patrizi, assicura che: «Non vi è ambascia, non vi è dolore, né agonia che il mio Dio pietosamente non me ne faccia amplissimo dono»; ed alle sue care Figlie: «Procuriamo dunque di andare passo passo facendo la strada sua (di Gesù): patire, faticare, negare se stessi per fare in ogni cosa la volontà dell'Eterno Dio».

M. Rosa, assistita dalla grazia di Dio, continuò il suo cammino, sicura che il Signore non l'avrebbe mai abbandonata, e seppe trasmettere questa sua serena fortezza nella prova, questa sua incrollabile fiducia nell'aiuto di Dio alle sue carissime Figlie, come è facile verificare attraverso l'edificante lettura delle lettere, dove non soltanto le Figlie di S. Anna, ma quanti avranno l'opportunità di leggerle, impareranno le virtù evangeliche: umiltà, povertà, pazienza, diligenza, franchezza, obbedienza, fortezza, serenità... il tutto unito a un grande amore alla preghiera, amore al patire, desiderio di essere umiliata, spirito di raccoglimento, devozione a Gesù Crocifisso e alla Madonna, ecc.

Mi congratulo con le dilettissime Figlie di S. Anna per questo nuovo volume delle lettere della Madre Fondatrice, vero dono di Dio, autentico regalo dello Spirito, e, direi pure, prezioso monumento alla santità vissuta e realizzata da M. Rosa, vera «donna forte» che seppe essere sempre aperta alla divina grazia e seppe vivere con costante e amorosa fiducia abbandonata come figlia nelle braccia di Dio. Con la pubblicazione del presente volume esse avranno a portata di mano uno strumento utilissimo per conoscere in profondità lo spirito evangelico di M. Rosa e, come accennavo all'inizio di questa mia presentazione, leggendo le sue lettere si metteranno in sintonia amorosa e profonda con «i suoi ideali, le sue aspirazioni, il suo pensiero, la sua brama di lavorare instancabilmente per la gloria di Dio, il servizio della Chiesa ed il bene dei fratelli».

INTRODUZIONE

Il presente volume viene a completare il blocco dell'epistolario del quadriennio 1871-1874 che, come si è evidenziato in Lettere, 2, (p. 18), si caratterizza per una fondamentale unità storica e carismatica. Le lettere di questo periodo esprimono infatti l'evoluzione iniziale della Famiglia nella concretizzazione strutturale delle comunità e dei servizi caritativi e la tensione spirituale di Madre Rosa originata dall'ardente desiderio di vedere la Famiglia inserita nella «vita e nella santità della Chiesa» mediante l'approvazione delle Regole; approvazione che aveva creduto di ottenere con facilità e rapidità e che fu invece, per il ponderato e prudente esame che caratterizza i criteri seguiti ordinariamente dalla Chiesa, difficile e protratta per anni. Ritardo che a lei invece riesce incomprensibile e non esente da interventi ostili al bene: «Invece di favorire l'Opera di Dio la si incatena».

L'esplosivo sviluppo dell'Istituto

L'ansiosa esigenza che muove la Madre a chiedere tempestivamente l'approvazione è la consapevolezza di aver agito nell'Opera di Dio per espresso comando del Santo Padre Pio IX. «È lui il vero fondatore».

È vero che la chiara coscienza del dono dello Spirito è di essersi lasciata guidare dallo Spirito: «Io tutto ho messo nelle mani di Dio... La volontà di Dio solo voglio, e in questa desidero morire» (L 93); vuole essere tuttavia confermata nel cammino intrapreso, vuole l'Opera di Dio segnata dal sigillo della Chiesa, perché possa essere sottratta a qualsiasi condizionamento che ne ostacoli lo sviluppo e le impedisca di estendersi in tutto il mondo «come volo di colomba». Non era stato questo il vaticinio del suo S. Padre Pio IX?

Vede chiaramente, d'altra parte le Regole come espressione genuina e fedele del carisma, della sua concezione di vita, oltre che frutto della sua esperienza, e strumento indispensabile che veicola lo spirito e la vita della Famiglia nelle giovani chiamate a farne parte. Il «ragionevole» ritardo della Chiesa nelTapprovarle le è pena dolorosissima: «Non si può certo credere quanta pena non mi reca quest'affare, avendo tante religiose da ammaestrare in questo spirito e senza niente, né in stampa, né in manoscritto, glielo domando per pietà» (al Segretario della S. Congregazione dei Vescovi e Regolari - L 76 -). Una pena unita ai tanti pati-

menti fisici e morali: «Senza forze, carica di dolori dalla testa i piedi, immersa nelle angosce...un andare passo passo facendo la strada sua

(di Gesù); patire, faticare, negare se stessi per fare in ogni cosa la volontà dell'Eterno Padre» "(L 42).

Umanamente è «uno straccio», pure è quasi sempre in viaggio lungo «la strada sua». Una scorsa rapida alle lettere in edizione ci offre il cronogramma del suo itinerario attraverso l'Italia settentrionale e centrale nei luoghi ove già sono o iniziano la loro presenza le Figlie di S. Anna. «Il 1872 mi tiene incatenata — aveva confidato a Sr. A. Francesca Camisa da Ferrara, dove attendeva alla compilazione delle nuove Regole — ma non sarà così il 1873». L'alba del nuovo anno la trova a Genova, ad animare le Sorelle nel ritiro annuale degli Esercizi Spirituali; si reca poi in visita alla Casa di Sampierdarena; il 13 gennaio si mette in viaggio per Roma. Una breve sosta a Piacenza, dove l'attende Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino per accompagnarla; una tappa di vari giorni a Foligno, per la fondazione di una nuova Casa. Tra mille difficoltà, incomprensioni e sospetti (L 9), «il diavoletto già incomincia a mettere la coda e a farmi disperare» (L 11) e inaudite sofferenze fisiche: «Sto tanto male che Iddio solo vede ciò che soffro... ho tanti dolori che tutti i momenti mi veniva da svenire» (L 12), riesce ad avviare la nuova opera (cf Indice IV). Il 24 è a Roma. Riaffronta senza indugio il problema che le sta a cuore più di ogni altro: l'approvazione delle Regole. Anche qui l'attendono dispiaceri a fatiche: «Questa mattina ho la testa che mi vacilla, quanti dispiaceri! Mi sento morire. Iddio voglia che resista... qui si tratta di nuovo del nostro nome (di Figlie di S. Anna), che orrore! Un diavolo che sta sotto che fa fuoco» (L 28).

Ha risposto intanto positivamente alla richiesta del Presidente dell'ospedale di Ovada (AL) (L 17) e si dà premura di istruire la Superiora Francesca Camisa inviandola ad accompagnare le Suore ed a fermarsi con loro tutto il tempo necessario all'impostazione e al buon funzionamento del servizio ospedaliero. Si rende presente nelle altre comunità mediante la corrispondenza interessandosi ai piccoli e grossi problemi quotidiani, consigliando le superiore e intervenendo direttamente per corrispondenza presso le autorità locali per le faccende connesse con l'ambito di loro competenza. Intanto anche a Roma la chiamano da più parti perché intervenga con le sue Suore in situazioni di impellenti necessità. Le Dame del «Circolo Cattolico S. Monica» riescono in breve ad offrirle quella sia pur minima collaborazione per effettuare ciò che desidera da anni. «Mi fu data una casa qui, nella Città santa, in Roma, onde aprirvi due scuole esterne e l'assistenza ai poveri infermi a domicilio» (al Vescovo Ranza, Piacenza, - L 44 -). Una casa: poche e nude stanzette

messe a disposizione dalla Marchesa Maddalena Galleffi, Superiora delle Oblate di Tor de' Specchi, accanto al Monastero (L 38). Tra marzo e aprile avvia in Roma quattro comunità, il che comporta gran movimento di Suore e per lei moltiplicato lavoro, tra difficoltà e preoccupazioni. Si rende pure necessaria nello stesso periodo la sua presenza a Foligno ed ogni volta le viene riservata una buona dose di assenzio: «Anche questa mattina ne ho abbastanza degli spasimi, che ne presi un altro poche ore sono; basta, per amor di Dio tutto è poco»: anche l'aperta e ostile insidia di male intenzionati sicari, anche il tentativo di incendio della casa (L 60; 62). Tutto è poco per chi ama.

Dopo sei mesi lascia Roma, non senza essersi prima recata, attorniata dalle sue figlie «romane» dal S. Padre a ricevere con la benedizione, la sua parola autorevole che le infonde sicurezza per l'avvenire dell'Opera. Il viaggio di ritorno è intervallato da una prima tappa a Foligno protrattasi oltre il previsto, poi a Firenze dove «combina l'accettazione di una casa da aprirsi in agosto», a Bologna accetta altre due case. Finalmente, a Piacenza. «Trovai — scrive a P. R. Bianchi, colui che sta rivedendo le Regole — un mezzo paese: ragazze, postulanti, religiose, tutto in ordine ed in pace con esatta osservanza» (L 114). Come, e più del solito, è stremata: «Questa volta la debolezza non vuole più lasciarmi, l'affanno è diminuito, ma le forze sono affatto perdute, non reggo in piedi per niente» (a P. A. Donadio - L 117 -). Pure continua a lavorare. «Chi mi regge?» si chiede stupita. La sua risposta è l'abbandono in accresciuta consapevolezza e fiducia nel caro Padre Eterno: «Fate, fate quello che volete, mio Dio, sono contenta e come un agnello alle poppe di sua madre mi trovo tranquilla» (L 99). Dalla pace profonda di questa sua immersione pacificante in Dio, sempre più cooptata per l'Opera che Egli le affida, si rafforza l'impegno del suo donarsi: «Per l'Opera sua si deve andare senza risparmio. Dunque, esso per noi diede tutto il suo sangue e noi così dobbiamo fare, sangue per sangue» (L 135); e dal suo darsi «sangue per sangue» sgorga la fecondità dell'Opera di Dio. Lei la vede crescere, fiorire e fruttificare: la casa di Piacenza è riempita di religiose e postulanti (L 180).

Le tante giovani che continuano ad arrivare a Casa Madre, indirizzate dai Parroci e altre persone o attirate alla Famiglia attraverso la testimonianza di Madre Rosa e delle sue figlie sono il segno luminoso di quella fecondità, come lo sono le tante nuove case che vanno sorgendo.

In ogni chiamata, da qualunque parte o da qualunque persona venga: Vescovi, Parroci, Sacerdoti, Presidenti di Opere Pie o laici desiderosi di promuovere il bene, avverte la voce stessa di Dio che le indica dove andare; ed ogni richiesta fa scattare in lei la molla della carità che urge.

E non si lascia condizionare da alcuna difficoltà di ordine pratico, né ama lungaggini procedurali. Espone le proprie condizioni per l'impianto dell'opera, in verità tanto poche da non scoraggiare nessuno: almeno quattro suore, un'abitazione «piccola» fornita del puro necessario, un contributo minimo in denaro (Lett. 17, 48, 98, 127, ecc.). Aliena da ogni ombra di interesse terreno, si ispira unicamente ai criteri evangelici e guarda Gesù Cristo: «Mio Salvatore! Voi che predicavate allo scoperto, voi senza casa, senza tetto, altro non avevate che la glorificazione del Padre Vostro, e noi? Quanto mi duole il sempre sentire che per fare un po' di bene ci vogliono comodi!» (L 338). «Prudenza sì, ma non una prudenza come questa del giorno d'oggi, che per fare un poco di carità bisogna che noi religiosi veniamo pagati in cima di casa. Che orrore, brutto spirito» (L 234).

II DONO e i doni

Questo fugace approccio alla lettura trasversale del presente volume nell'ottica della espansione dell'Istituto è un semplice avvio e vuol essere invito alla continuazione e all'approfondimento. Lo concludiamo col linguaggio dei numeri, di per sé incisivo e significativo. All'inizio del 1873 le case sono 7, alla fine 17; al termine del 1874 se ne registrano 24. Nel 1873 ricevono l'abito delle Figlie di S. Anna 53 Novizie, nel 1874, 83.

A questa tematica dell'espansione dell'Istituto, rilevante nei risvolti: vocazionale, operativo, culturale, storico, ne sono compresenti altre, non meno importanti. Anzitutto la figura poliedrica di Madre Rosa nelle varie sfaccettature della sua personalità come donna, religiosa, fondatrice, le sue caratteristiche psicologiche, le linee della sua pedagogia come educatrice delle Figlie di S. Anna; i suoi rapporti con le varie personalità, le amicizie; Madre Rosa e la Chiesa col connesso problema del riconoscimento giuridico; Padre Tornatore e la sua presenza nell'Istituto; i più stretti collaboratori ecclesiastici e laici, ecc.

Uno studio prolungato e approfondito «con intelletto d'amore» porterebbe a scoperte feconde di conoscenza e di appropriazione del DONO e dei doni dello Spirito nelle persone di M. Rosa, P. Tornatore, nella vita della Famiglia da essi generata per volere del Padre e nella fecondità dello Spirito come risposta di peculiare vita evangelica nella Chiesa, al seguito di Cristo povero.
